why_relevant: Referenced by Erste Group as the procurement unit's own website; the likely host of the online procurement platform / supplier entry point used for Erste Bank Hungary sourcing. Not fetched in this pass — URL recorded for the deterministic liveness pass.

entity_name: Magyar Fintech Szövetség / Hungarian Fintech Association
why_relevant: Industry association bundling HU fintech/payments actors; member listings and position papers are a compact actor map and a route to PSPs/TPPs that never appear in procurement portals.

source_name: ÁSZ közérdekű adatok – saját szerződések és beszerzések
why_relevant: ÁSZ itself publishes its service-procurement and asset-sale contracts above the statutory threshold, and its own management is audited by an auditor selected through public procurement — a small but concrete example of the public-body contract-disclosure layer that also applies to banking service contracts.

source_name: Commercial IFI tender aggregators (TendersOnTime, GlobalTenders, TendersInfo, BidDetail)
why_relevant: Paid aggregators re-index EBRD/EIB notices and sometimes surface items faster or with better country tagging than the primary portals. Useful only as a cross-check/backfill layer, never as a primary or citable source.

source_name: Erste Bank Hungary – Visszaélés-bejelentő rendszer az Erste Csoport partnerei számára
why_relevant: Partner/supplier-facing whistleblowing channel — confirms the existence of a formal supplier-relationship compliance layer at Erste Bank Hungary and is a leading indicator of supplier-governance changes (a channel like this is usually created alongside supplier code enforcement).

source_name: LinkedIn company pages of Hungarian banking/fintech associations
why_relevant: Association and chamber LinkedIn pages publish event announcements, sponsor tags and partner mentions that are often not mirrored on the main websites, and surface the individuals brokering vendor-bank relationships.
Secondary aggregators/consultancies; their public blog and category pages sometimes surface individual notices and buyer names that help snowball the actor map, even without subscribing.

source_name: Bizpay.hu blog (online payment / POS vendor blog)
why_relevant: Vendor-operated Hungarian blog on online payment and POS terminals; useful for terminology, merchant-side pain points and competitor positioning in card acceptance. Vendor bias must be flagged.

Founding member of the Hungarian Blockchain Coalition and consortium member of the DigitalTech EDIH project; its partner and coalition affiliations point to public-sector-facing digital consortia that bid for or shape state and financial-sector digital tenders.

source_name: County chamber registered-business databases (BOKIK, DKIK et al.)
why_relevant: Regional chambers expose the chamber registry through their own searchable front-ends, sometimes with different filters/exports than the national portal. Useful fallback for identifying and geolocating suppliers named in award notices.

source_name: EU Publications Office — public procurement procurement-details pages (op.europa.eu)
why_relevant: Publications Office mirrors individual procurement records (observed pattern .../procurement-details/-/procurement/{uuid}) and hosts TED reusers-workshop material explaining how to retrieve eForms notices — both a data surface and a methodology source.

Hungarian consultancy-run tender monitoring product. Adds vendor diversity to the HU aggregator map and, as a consultancy, its published references and case pages can indirectly reveal which Hungarian buyers and suppliers are active in IT/financial-services procurement.

Secondary aggregator that surfaces ads from smaller Hungarian boards and staffing firms not indexed by Profession; useful redundancy for catching short-lived contractor postings tied to a delivery ramp-up.

Surfaced alongside kozadat.hu as a Hungarian public-data aggregation site; potentially a secondary index of közérdekű adat disclosures. Listed as a lead to be assessed — its operator, scope and freshness were not established in this pass.

Aggregates Közbeszerzési Értesítő + TED + additional Hungarian buyer sourcing pages into one searchable database; an alternative commercial cross-check with different coverage of non-Kbt. buyer notices.

entity_name: Magyar Posta supplier bidding via SAP Ariba Sourcing
source_name: Magyar Posta supplier bidding via SAP Ariba Sourcing
why_relevant: Posta's notices state that detailed tender conditions and bid submission run through SAP Ariba Sourcing with mandatory supplier registration — meaning the substantive documentation is behind a supplier login, which caps what open collection can see and is itself an intelligence fact about access.

source_name: Magyar Telekom beszerzési portál (szállítói regisztráció) – structural comparator
why_relevant: Not a bank, but the reference implementation of a fully public Hungarian corporate supplier portal (versenyfelhívások = published RFx, szállítói regisztráció, működési kódex, named lead buyers). It defines the Hungarian vocabulary and the structural template to look for at banks, and shows exactly what Hungarian banks do NOT publish.

source_name: palyazatok.org / cegpalyazat.hu - grant-programme trackers (POS & supplier development)
why_relevant: Grant trackers reveal state-funded demand for POS terminals and supplier-development budgets, which drive terminal-estate procurement volumes at acquirers - a weak but early demand signal.

English-language aggregator entry for the Hungarian FinTechShow with dates, agenda and venue metadata; useful as an independent cross-check and for building an EN-side event calendar when the Hungarian organiser site is JS-blocked.

Corporate-side announcements of the upcoming conference season give forward calendar visibility (which banking/payments events will run and when), enabling scheduled harvesting of sponsor lists at publication time.

One of the older Hungarian grant/tender portals with an established free public feed of calls. Useful as a redundancy source and for older archived calls that newer commercial platforms may not retain.

Hungarian pályázatfigyelő (grant/tender watch) service. Grant-side monitoring gives upstream signal on funded modernisation programmes that later convert into banking/payments procurement, complementing the notice-side aggregators.

Additional Hungarian tender-services provider surfaced by local-language search. Included for completeness of the HU vendor map; usefulness for banking/payments specifically is unconfirmed and its offering was not inspected in depth.

source_name: TenderMonitor (kozbeszerzesmonitor.hu) / Napitender / InnoTender - HU monitoring vendors
why_relevant: Cluster of Hungarian tender-monitoring vendors covering all national and EU sources with unlimited-keyword subscriptions. Relevant mainly as coverage benchmarks and as a shortcut to keyword taxonomies that Hungarian bidders actually use for banking/payments lots.

Reseller and comparison sites enumerate which acquirers, terminal hardware brands and gateways are actively sold in Hungary and at what pricing — a fast, if commercially biased, map of the merchant-facing supply side and of switching offers.

Entry point to UniCredit group-level corporate systems; relevant as the identified access surface for group supplier/tender interactions, though authenticated. Useful mainly to document that UniCredit's Hungarian vendor pipeline is behind a group login rather than any public notice board.
